# Fanfarr v0.4.0

Fanfarr finds theme music for a Plex library, writes it beside the media as a
local `theme.mp3`, and keeps a permanent record of what it did and why. This is
the first release since v0.3.1, and most of it is about not losing that record.

## Backups, and getting one back

The database is everything Fanfarr knows: your settings, the mirror of Plex, the
ThemerrDB cache, and the append-only record of every theme it has written.
Nothing else on disk can reconstruct it -- Plex cannot be asked what Fanfarr
did. There was no copy of it anywhere.

There is now. Snapshots are taken on a schedule -- daily by default, seven kept
-- into `<config>/backups/`, using SQLite's own `VACUUM INTO`: safe while the
application is running, compacted, and no `sqlite3` binary involved.

**Backups** in Settings holds all of it: the switch, the interval, how many to
keep, what they cost in disk, how old the newest is, and **Back up now**, which
works even with the schedule off, because off means not *automatically* rather
than never. Any snapshot can be downloaded, which is how a copy leaves the
machine that made it.

**Restore** puts one back. It takes a `pre-restore` snapshot of the current
state first, keeps the database it replaced as `fanfarr.db.replaced-<time>`, and
applies the swap on the next start rather than immediately -- SQLite keeps its
write-ahead log beside the database, and replacing that file under a running
application is how you lose both. A snapshot kept on another machine can be
uploaded instead, which is the way back when the disk that held the snapshots is
the thing that failed.

Three rules keep it honest, and each has a test behind it: a snapshot is
verified before it is announced, so a partial file from a full disk cannot be
listed as a backup; only files Fanfarr wrote are ever deleted by the rotation, so
a database you copied in by hand survives; and nothing a restore does can stop
the container starting, because a container that will not start can only be fixed
by hand.

## Leave a title alone

**Exclude** on the library's bulk bar, or the toggle on an item page, marks a
title as one that nothing unattended should touch. It stops counting as missing
and stops being picked by a bulk apply. A trim or an apply you ask for by hand
still runs: the flag governs what happens on its own.

This closes a gap that had no workaround at all. Until now, leaving one show
alone meant disabling its whole library.

## Security

`mix hex.audit` now runs in CI, where it fails the build rather than telling
nobody, and Dependabot proposes the bumps. The first run found two advisories,
one hidden behind the other: `lazy_html` (test-only, so never in the image) and
**Ash itself**, where private action arguments could be set from user input on
the bulk destroy and update paths. Both are fixed in this release.

## Also

- The documentation claimed a dry run existed and was the default. It was removed
  in v0.1.51 along with its column. Applying a theme writes a local file and
  never uploads, and the one upload path is the System page's per-item
  diagnostic. The documentation now says what the code does.

## Upgrading

Pull the new image and restart; the database migrates itself on boot. Three
things worth knowing:

- Backups start as soon as you upgrade, with the schedule on. Settings >
  Backups has the switch, and **Back up now** takes one immediately.
- No existing title is excluded, so nothing changes for them: the column arrives
  with the migration, off.
- Snapshots land in `<config>/backups/`, on the same volume as the database. That
  protects against a mistake, not against the disk failing. Download a copy
  somewhere else, or point `BACKUP_DIR` at another disk.
